from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Change", [
            "Derivative measures the cat's instantaneous speed.",
            "Integral tracks the cat's total distance covered.",
            "Speed is slope; distance is area."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        grid_bg = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[0, 6, 1], y_range=[0, 6, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#555555", "stroke_width": 1}
        )
        self.place_in_area(grid_bg, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        cat_point = Dot(color="#4287f5", radius=0.1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#4287f5")
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_bg))
        self.play(Create(cat_point.move_to(self.grid["F1"])))
        self.play(cat_point.animate.move_to(self.grid["A6"]), run_time=3)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#4287f5")
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#4287f5")
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Accumulating rate yields the original function.", 
                         "Small rectangles create the growing area.", 
                         "Integration undoes the derivative process."]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Inverse Relationship", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define elements
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], x_length=4, y_length=4, axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve1 = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * x**2, color="#ff9800")
        curve2 = axes.plot(lambda x: x, color="#00bcd4")
        
        # Container for right side display
        right_side = VGroup(axes, curve1, curve2)
        self.place_in_area(right_side, "A2", "F5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        arrow = Arrow(start=RIGHT, end=LEFT, color="#ffffff")
        self.place_at_grid(arrow, "C3", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        circle = Circle(radius=0.1, color="#ffffff", fill_opacity=0)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#ff9800"))
        self.play(Create(curve1), Create(curve2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00bcd4"))
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow))
        self.play(Rotate(arrow, angle=PI/2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#ffffff"))
        self.play(circle.animate.set_fill(opacity=1))
        self.play(Flash(circle.get_center(), color="#ffffff"))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Fundamental Theorem of Calculus", [
            "Antiderivatives link slopes to total area.",
            "Subtract boundaries to find net change.",
            "It simplifies complex summation tasks."
        ])

        # Define axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A2", "D5", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        func = lambda x: 0.25 * x**2
        curve = axes.plot(func, color="#8bc34a")
        
        # Area filler
        area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, 3], color="#fff176", opacity=0.5)
        
        # Integral label
        integral = MathTex(r"\int_a^b f(x) \, dx", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(integral, "E3", scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#8bc34a")
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.play(FadeIn(area))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#fff176")
        self.play(Write(integral))
        
        # Animate moving b
        b_val = ValueTracker(3)
        def get_area():
            return axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, b_val.get_value()], color="#fff176", opacity=0.5)
        
        area_updater = always_redraw(get_area)
        self.add(area_updater)
        self.play(b_val.animate.set_value(4), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#ffffff")
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis and Application", [
            "Slopes transform into area evaluations.",
            "Geometric problems become simple subtraction.",
            "Synthesis reveals calculus's fundamental bridge."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture_texts[0].set_color("#ffffff")
        
        # Complex system diagram nodes
        nodes = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3) for _ in range(4)])
        self.place_at_grid(nodes[0], 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(nodes[1], 'B5')
        self.place_at_grid(nodes[2], 'E2')
        self.place_at_grid(nodes[3], 'E5')
        
        connections = VGroup(
            Line(nodes[0].get_center(), nodes[1].get_center()),
            Line(nodes[1].get_center(), nodes[3].get_center()),
            Line(nodes[3].get_center(), nodes[2].get_center()),
            Line(nodes[2].get_center(), nodes[0].get_center())
        )
        self.add(connections, nodes)
        self.play(Create(nodes), Create(connections))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture_texts[0].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture_texts[1].set_color("#ff4081")
        
        # Signal flow (glowing pulse)
        pulse = Circle(radius=0.1, color="#ff4081", fill_opacity=1)
        self.add(pulse)
        for i in range(len(connections)):
            self.play(MoveAlongPath(pulse, connections[i]), run_time=0.8)
        self.remove(pulse)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture_texts[1].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture_texts[2].set_color("#ffc107")
        
        # Highlight final result (gold square)
        result_box = Square(color="#ffc107", stroke_width=4)
        self.place_in_area(result_box, 'B2', 'E5')
        self.play(Create(result_box))
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Bridge Between Slopes and Areas: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Change
sections.content: Briefly review the derivative as 'instantaneous rate of change' (slope) and the integral as 'accumulation' (area under a curve). Use a visualization of a moving car’s speedometer (rate) versus the odometer (distance).
sections.example: A cat running: The speedometer shows how fast the cat is at any second (derivative); the distance traveled by the cat over time is the area under that speed-time graph (integral).

sections.title: Visualizing the Inverse Relationship
sections.content: Introduce the core insight: If you accumulate area under a rate function, you get back to the original function. Use an animation showing a growing 'shaded area' rectangle whose height is defined by f(x) and width by dx.
sections.example: Imagine filling a bucket with water (integration). The rate at which the water level rises (derivative) is exactly the speed at which you are pouring it in. Doing one 'undoes' the other.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part 1 & 2)
sections.content: Formally connect the two: If F'(x) = f(x), then the integral of f(x) from a to b equals F(b) - F(a). Emphasize that finding the area is as simple as evaluating the antiderivative at the boundaries.
sections.example: If a robot moves with velocity v(t) = 2t, we find its position function s(t) = t² + C. To find the distance moved from t=1 to t=3, we simply calculate s(3) - s(1) = 9 - 1 = 8.

sections.title: Synthesis and Application
sections.content: Show a side-by-side animation: Left side shows the tangent line sliding along a curve (derivative); right side shows the integral sign transforming into the evaluation brackets [F(x)]_a^b.
sections.example: Using the Theorem to find the exact area of a parabolic arch that a drone flies over, simplifying a complex summation problem into a basic subtraction problem.
